messages:
pagerduty-bot: Page triggered: HIGH - 'gpu-prefill-oom' on prod-serving-cluster (alerts: gpu-memory-usage > 95%)

olivia: seeing repeated container restarts on srv-gpu-prod-12 in us-west1. Pods getting OOMKilled during prefill for long-context requests. Customer-facing latency/failures ramping. tagging @sam, @matt

sam: on it. grabbing pod logs now. initial triage: looks like very long system prompts + 2-3 meg token prefill for some requests. suspect prefill alloc spikes the KV cache and exceeds GPU memory.

sam: kubectl get pods -n serving | grep srv-gpu-prod-12
```
```
POD                          READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
inference-abc-123            1/1     OOMKilled 5          2h
inference-def-456            1/1     Running   0          12h
```
```

sam: logs from inference-abc-123 show CUDA OOM during attention prefill: 
```
```
RuntimeError: CUDA error: out of memory
  File "/opt/runtime/prefill.py", line 312, in run_prefill
    kv_cache = alloc_kv_cache(batch_size, total_prefill_tokens)
  File "/opt/runtime/memory.py", line 89, in alloc_kv_cache
    raise RuntimeError("CUDA OOM")
```

olivia: ok mitigation ideas — rank by impact: 1) short-term reject/prevent huge prefill requests at gateway, 2) fallback to smaller model variant when prefill > X, 3) tune prefill_batch_size and KV cache allocation so we fail earlier and avoid container restarts, 4) cordon node if restarts are noisy.

matt: i'm going to push a quick gateway rule to reject prefill > 200k tokens and return 413 to clients. also enabling a safety throttle for simultaneous large-prefill workloads. will run canary in us-west1 with 10% traffic.

matt: applying patch (hotfix):
```
```
# curl to control plane patch (pseudo)
curl -X PATCH https://console.internal/api/v1/gateway/config \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OP' \
  -d '{"prefill_limits": {"max_tokens": 200000, "reject_response": 413}, "large_prefill_concurrency": 2}'
```
```

eng-runtime-bot: Deploy started for gateway-config-hotfix by matt. Canaries: us-west1 (10%), rollout: auto if checks pass.

sam: while the hotfix rolls, I set a short-lived admission controller rule on the serving namespace to annotate pods with oom-watch and increased restart backoff to avoid thrashing. kubectl patch deployment inference --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"oom-watch":"true"}}}}}' -n serving

nina: tracking customer impact: 14k requests failed with 5xx in last 30m, two customers reported visible errors (acct-342, acct-998). CS alerted those accounts and offered temporary mitigation suggestions.

olivia: good. making on-call handoff to eng-runtime for deep dive. sam please keep runbook notes in the incident board and open a follow-up ticket with metrics: per-model prefill token distribution, per-node memory spikes, and a sample of offending requests (sanitized).

sam: will do. created INC-2026-873 in our tracker and added initial notes + logs.

matt: can confirm canary passing (no new OOMs on canary nodes), gateway now returning 413 for oversized prefill requests. rolling to 100% in 2m.

eng-runtime-bot: Deploy succeeded: gateway-config-hotfix v1.2.3 -> 100% traffic.

olivia: running a gradual node drain of srv-gpu-prod-12 to stop thrashing and give SRE a stable baseline for heap inspection. cordoned node, moving pods.

sam: quick mitigation summary I'm putting in the incident chat log: 
- root cause: extremely large prefill token allocations (rare long prompts) cause KV cache allocation to spike and exceed GPU memory.
- mitigation: gateway prefill size limit (200k tokens), concurrency throttles for large-prefill jobs, increased container restart backoff, canary rollout of config.
- impact: transient 5xx errors and some container restarts; two customers reported errors; no data loss.

nina: CS update sent to impacted customers with ETA for a postmortem. will coordinate with eng-runtime for next-day customer-facing summary.

olivia: handing off to eng-runtime (sam/matt) for root-cause analysis and postmortem. SRE will collect dmesg/kern logs and GPU memory traces; eng-runtime to produce remediation plan (kernel-level memory accounting + better prefill admission).

sam: noted — will pull historical prefill distributions and propose two follow-ups: 1) runtime-level early rejection if estimated prefill memory > 70% of device, 2) model-serving hint to prefer KV-compressed variants for large contexts.

matt: i'll own the short-term ticket to add metric-based OOM alerts that factor in prefill token estimates (not just GPU memory).

olivia: thanks team. creating postmortem ticket and assigning to sam/matt. closing incident channel once postmortem is linked. :white_check_mark:

eng-runtime-bot: Incident INC-2026-873 acknowledged and transitioned to 'postmortem required' state.

nina: final note — recorded customer impact numbers and CS outreach. will update customers after postmortem review.

olivia: all — great fast work. if anyone finds suspicious regressions in the next 24h ping me directly.
